title: Associated graded rings determine the dimension of a Noetherian local ring
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak n)$ and $(T,\mathfrak p)$ be commutative Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $I\subseteq\mathfrak n$ and $J\subseteq\mathfrak p$ be ideals. Form the nonnegatively graded rings
$$\operatorname{gr}_I(R)=\bigoplus_{q\ge0}I^q/I^{q+1},\qquad \operatorname{gr}_J(T)=\bigoplus_{q\ge0}J^q/J^{q+1},$$
with multiplication induced by ideal multiplication and degree-zero parts $R/I$ and $T/J$. If these are isomorphic as graded rings, then $\dim R=\dim T$, where dimension is Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Zero ideals are allowed; the ideals need not be primary for the maximal ideals.

source.place: Expose III Corollary 5.4(i) and its proof, pp.42--43: the dimension at a point of the closed subscheme equals the dimension at the zero section of its normal cone (Matsumura, Commutative Ring Theory, Theorem 15.9, as cited there). This is its local-ring formulation for arbitrary ideals contained in the maximal ideals, used for each boundary intersection in the final paragraph of III Proposition 6.2, pp.44--45.
